still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates and still lists branded Wegovy pill starting doses at $149 a month, now beside a cheaper authorised-generic line.
Eli Lilly still leads on efficacy, and no oral drug matches tirzepatide.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in 2026 is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands.
Tirzepatide's August 2028 dementia-risk indication is still on the label, its postmarketing confirmatory trial is still unreported, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums still stands.

population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. Cycling arithmetic: 24.5% ever-used minus 17.0% current = 7.5% of adults who have used the drugs and are off them now. 44% of ever-users have cycled = 10.8 points. About 9.0 points are current users on at least their second course (53% of current users, up from 46%, because ~0.6M Bridge lapsers and many gray-market quitters restarted on the subsidised generic). About 1.8 points are cyclers who are off again. That fits roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, compounded over more cycles. Headcount: 17.0% of ~267M adults ≈ 45.4M current users. FICTIONAL payer mix at Dec 2030: Medicare ~27% (~12.4M: ~8M carried over on diabetes, cardiovascular, CKD, sleep-apnoea and dementia codes, ~1.4M added on those codes, and ~3.0M on the new obesity benefit since Apr 2030); Medicaid ~13% (~6.0M); HRSA free provision at health centres ~3% (~1.4M uninsured). Public total ~44% (~19.8M), the largest payer bloc. Commercial ~26% (~11.8M), legitimate cash ~22.5% (~10.2M), gray market and counterfeit ~8% (~3.6M, down from a ~5M peak in late 2029). Age check: 18–29 (20% of adults × 9%) + 30–49 (33% × 15.5%) + 50–64 (24% × 26%) + 65+ (23% × 17%) ≈ 17.1%. Income check: thirds of ~89M adults at 20/16/15% ≈ 17.8M + 14.2M + 13.4M = 45.4M. The bottom-third rate rose 11 → 15% on Medicaid's enhanced match and health-centre provision. The top-third rate fell 21 → 20% as some older affluent users stopped on bone advice or moved to 'lift-first' programmes. Adult obesity is ~33.9%. About 23% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. They are concentrated in the 12 Medicaid non-opt-in states, among uninsured adults far from health centres, and among people who refuse. Under-18 use is ~0.9%, mostly ages 12–17. It rose on Medicaid adolescent coverage of the generic, and the bone warning slowed it. Upper-income adolescent use flattened at about 1 in 5 of those with severe obesity.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Lower Cost Metabolic Care Act (Dec 2029 year-end package). (1) Part D covers obesity treatment from Apr 2030, but only for the generic tier (authorised-generic semaglutide, oral or pen) at a $0–10 copay. Branded tirzepatide and retatrutide stay behind diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnoea and dementia prior authorisation. For 65+ users continuing past 12 months, coverage requires a documented DXA and resistance-training or protein counselling referral. CBO arithmetic: ~5M average added obesity users × $55 net × 12 ≈ $3.3B/yr, plus ~$0.4B DXA and counselling, ≈ $37B over 2030–39 gross. Offsets of ~$18B from bill-attributable brand-to-generic switching and ~$1B medical offsets give ≈ $18B net. The 2027 permanent benefit had been scored at ~$41B. (2) Medicaid gets a 90% federal match for generic incretins: ~6.0M users × $55 × 12 ≈ $4.0B/yr, of which ~$3.6B is federal. 38 states plus DC cover; 12 do not. Two still tie coverage to adherence and BMI at 6 and 12 months. (3) HRSA Metabolic Health Access gives the uninsured free generic semaglutide at federally qualified health centres: ~1.4M × $55 × 12 ≈ $0.92B/yr against a $1B/yr appropriation.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide now costs $5–30/month across 80+ brands, and Chinese makers have added generic liraglutide and semaglutide at scale. Generics are approved in ~175 countries. India and China supply most of the world's semaglutide. Chinese 'research-grade' tirzepatide and retatrutide powders are the new export growth line.
access.note: FICTIONAL. 'Generic' in the US means a Novo-made authorised generic of semaglutide, launched Jan 2030 under an HHS agreement: 25 mg pill and pen, $49–69/month cash via TrumpRx and pharmacies, $55 net to public payers. No ANDA generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the market. Patent settlements allow licensed ANDA entry (Viatris, Dr. Reddy's, Sandoz and others) from Mar 2031. Branded prices: Wegovy pill $149–299; Foundayo $149–299; Zepbound vials and pens $349–499 cash; retatrutide (Elevra) ~$1,050 cash with little coverage; survodutide ~$650. Orals are ~58% of total users and ~75% of new starts. Employer coverage rose 44% → 51% almost entirely as generic-only tiers. Brand coverage for weight alone is down to ~18% of employers. The gray market moved upmarket: semaglutide counterfeits largely collapsed against $49 legitimate product, while counterfeit Zepbound pens and 'research' retatrutide grew.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; authorised-generic pen from Jan 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; authorised-generic semaglutide tablet from Jan 2030)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide: Elevra, approved Mar 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Nov 2029, obesity only)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. ANDA generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide, Aug 2028; confirmatory trial pending)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth and EAPs; the oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out positive in 2030, but no sNDA decision has been made
dementia-prevention use without cardiovascular disease, now mostly on the $49 generic pill
microdosing and deliberate dose de-escalation to manage 'flatness'
nicotine, gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction: observational support only
gray-market 'research' retatrutide in gym and physique culture
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: No new indications this step. Approvals were new products or new forms of existing ones. Oral parity: in May 2029 a head-to-head trial found Foundayo (orforglipron) non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~14.6% vs ~15.3%), and the label was updated. Together with the 2027 Wegovy-pill result and the Jan 2030 authorised-generic tablet, that removed the needle as a barrier at every price point. No oral matches tirzepatide. Retatrutide (Lilly) was approved Mar 2029 at doses up to 9 mg (~24% mean loss). It carries a dysesthesia warning and a lean-mass monitoring recommendation, and the 12 mg dose was not approved. Survodutide (Boehringer Ingelheim) was approved Nov 2029 for obesity; its MASH sNDA is pending. Amycretin was filed Jun 2029, and its decision was extended to Q1 2031. MariTide (monthly) was filed Sep 2030 and is not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle-preserving adjuncts are still in phase 3 with none approved, which is the gap the bone wave exposes. Global incretin market ~$131B (2030): volume is up sharply, US net prices are falling, and Novo's US revenue fell even as its US unit volume roughly doubled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Health-centre starts on the generic pill show higher early drop-off where titration follow-up is thin.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; higher on retatrutide in proportion to loss.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now a recognised population problem. AHRQ/NCHS data (Mar 2030) show hip-fracture admissions among women 75+ rose ~3% from 2028 to 2030, reversing a decade of decline. Modelling attributes ~8,000–10,000 excess hip fractures a year to incretin use, against ~300,000 total. Risk is concentrated in women 65+, long-term users, repeated cyclers and low-protein users. Sarcopenia diagnoses in users 70+ are about 2.5× the 2025 level. Retatrutide's greater loss carries proportionally greater lean-mass loss in trials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D requires a DXA and a counselling referral for 65+ users continuing past 12 months. USPSTF draft (2030) recommends DXA for incretin users 65+ of either sex. The FDA class label was strengthened (2029) with a recommendation to consider dose reduction in sarcopenic patients. DXA wait times run 8–14 weeks in Florida and Arizona.

safety_ledger.effect: Sarcopenic frailty and falls in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare Advantage data show non-fracture fall-related ED visits ~15% higher among users 75+ after a year of use. Effects are confounded by the frailer population that the new benefit brought in.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS quality measure on falls screening for incretin users; Endocrine Society/AGS joint 'start low, lift first' guidance.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts are still conflicting; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA lists it among adverse reactions.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A prospective randomised substudy (2030, n≈3,400) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~8% of users versus ~3% on placebo. The effect is dose-related and mostly reverses within 6–8 weeks of dose reduction. Surveys suggest about a quarter of users report milder 'flatness'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Anhedonia added to adverse reactions (Jun 2030) with dose-reduction language; no boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles and disproportionately as fat. The 2028 Bridge lapsers are now the clearest documented cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; part of the chronic-therapy framing in the Part D benefit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency, especially among low-income users on reduced food budgets and those microdosing outside clinical care.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: HRSA protocol includes baseline labs; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents; effects of repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exists. The adolescent bone postmarketing study has enrolled but not reported. Medicaid adolescent coverage has widened the exposed group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density postmarketing requirement; AAP advises DXA at baseline and 12 months for adolescents.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in roughly 1 in 10 at higher doses in trials. Postmarketing reports are rising, especially from gray-market 'research' product taken at doses above the label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled warning; the 12 mg dose was not approved.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~14,000 cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product by late 2030. In Apr 2029, counterfeit Ozempic and Zepbound pens containing insulin caused a hypoglycaemia cluster of 63 hospitalisations and 3 deaths. Poison-centre calls peaked in 2029 at ~4× the 2025 level and have fallen since the $49 generic launched. Harms are now concentrated in counterfeit tirzepatide and 'research' retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alerts expanded to tirzepatide and retatrutide. CBP mail seizures are up ~4×. A 2029 settlement makes two major marketplaces delist peptide vendors. Personal importation enforcement is still porous.

food_and_beverage.state: About a third of US households now have a user. For the first time the volume decline reaches dollar-store and SNAP-heavy baskets, as Medicaid and health-centre provision bring in the bottom third. Snack and confectionery volume is down ~7–9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~7%. Dollar General and regional bottlers cite 'metabolic programme penetration' in guidance. Premium protein is now itself a class product: whey isolate and grass-fed lines at the top, fortified store-brand shakes at the bottom.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is down ~9% from 2025 and beer ~6%. Cheap generic access means heavy drinkers in lower-income regions can now get the drug. Brown-Forman and regional brewers have closed more capacity, and NA lines are now ~6% of beer volume. Bars in mid-sized Midwest cities keep shortening hours.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down at value chains; average checks are stable through small plates and protein add-ons. Buffets are largely gone outside casinos. Steakhouses and 'high-protein' fast-casual are the growth formats among affluent diners.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep consolidating. The class split shows in clothing. Upper-income buyers want tailored fits for 'lifted' bodies, and athletic brands sell 'density' lines. Mass retailers sell stretch fabrics for cyclers and for the softer thin body of generic users. Resale and rental absorb size churn.

fitness.state: Strength training is still the growth market, and it has split. Premium 'density clinics' bundle DXA, coaching and protein plans at $200–400/month. Medicare Advantage plans and YMCAs run 'lift-first' classes to meet the Part D counselling requirement. DXA chains are capacity-constrained.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend eased to ~+5% as plans moved to generic-first tiers. Adherence-verified programmes shrank from ~3M to ~1.8M enrollees after the California ban and EEOC settlement guidance. Medicare Part D plans price the new obesity benefit into 2031 bids. Medicare Advantage plans compete on DXA access.

pharma.state: Unit volumes are at record highs and US net prices are falling. Novo trades margin for public volume through the authorised generic: ~20M public users × $55 ≈ $13B/yr at thin margins. Lilly holds the premium tier with tirzepatide and retatrutide in cash and commercial channels. Indian firms prepare for licensed 2031 entry. Brand protection against counterfeit pens is a growing cost.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness alone no longer signals anything, because a $49 pill or a free health-centre bottle can produce it. Muscle density, posture and DXA scores now carry the signal. A thin, soft, slightly stooped body over 50 reads as 'state-issue'. A lean, dense one reads as money: tirzepatide or retatrutide, a coach, protein and scans.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The uniform changed from thin to dense. In Houston, 'Medicaid thin' is now a phrase in clinics and on social media, while River Oaks gyms sell 'density' memberships with quarterly DXA printouts that people share like marathon times. Older women in Florida are the visible casualty cohort, thin and fracturing. Lower-income users carry the regained-and-lost look of repeated cycling.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short. 'Skip days' have become a social convention: some households keep a no-pill Sunday for church dinners or family meals. Because semaglutide's half-life is about a week, an endocrinologist will tell you a skipped day barely changes anything, but it matters as ritual. The 'Bread Alone' fasting network claims ~500 congregations.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles now list body-composition goals more than drug status. 'Lifting partner' is a dating category. Desire mismatch is still a common therapy issue, now usually handled by negotiating doses. Couples schedule 'off weeks' around trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial rather than a sin or a symptom. People talk about their dose the way they talk about caffeine. The refusal coalition persists but has lost its 'pharma greed' argument now that the drug is cheap. It argues about sedation and bone instead.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2030 prospective substudy found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~8% of users versus ~3% on placebo. About a quarter of users report milder flatness. In 2030 surveys ~35% of oral users say they deliberately skip doses or step down a dose to 'feel more'.
interior_life.framing: A side effect, discussed as openly as SSRI flatness. 'Going grey' is the common phrase. Employers have mostly dropped 'steadiness' from their materials. Clinicians manage it with dose reduction. Talk shows run segments on 'finding your dose'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence-verified programmes have shrunk to ~1.8M enrollees. A 2030 EEOC conciliation agreement requires reasonable alternatives for anyone who reduces dose or stops for side effects. Some sales and creative employers quietly prefer staff who are 'off or low'. Call-centre and logistics employers still favour steadiness informally.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off nights' have spread from the Unmuted collective in Philadelphia and Brooklyn to club nights in Chicago and Atlanta. Comedians do 'skip day' material. Sportsbook handle per identifiable user is still lower, and operators target non-users. 'Flat' fiction has a counter-genre of 'thaw' memoirs about stepping down a dose.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Dose negotiation between partners is ordinary. Holiday and anniversary 'off weeks' are common, which feeds cycling and short regain-loss loops.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The coalition against adherence-conditioned premiums won in California in 2029. It is now split over whether free public provision is care or sedation. MAHA-aligned legislators attack the HRSA programme as 'pills instead of food' while their own constituents enrol. Turnout shows no measurable drug effect.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-volume and pro-speed: retatrutide and survodutide were approved, and the oral label was updated quickly. HHS combines 'food first' messaging with the largest public drug-provision programme since the Part D launch. Import enforcement has tightened on counterfeit pens but is still porous for personal mail.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Subsidy, not mandate. Part D covers obesity on the generic tier at a $0–10 copay. Medicaid gets a 90% federal match for generic incretins. HRSA gives free generic semaglutide to uninsured adults at health centres. No one is required to take it.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Part D continuation for users 65+ past 12 months requires a DXA and a counselling referral, which is a bone condition rather than an adherence condition. Two state Medicaid programmes still require adherence and BMI checks. Employer fill-verification survives outside Illinois and California under EEOC alternative-standard terms. PBM fill data still flow to wellness vendors under consent forms.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army made supervised oral semaglutide for recruits within 10% of the weight standard permanent (2029), with DXA at enlistment. TRICARE added the generic tier for weight management. DOT issued no rule on off-label alcohol-reduction use by drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Lower US prices weakened the Danish–US price quarrel and moved the dispute to counterfeits. US–India trade terms now include licensed 2031 generic entry, and US–China talks include peptide export controls on tirzepatide and retatrutide powders. Novo got tariff relief for US fill-finish capacity as part of the authorised-generic deal.

events.event: CDC links counterfeit Ozempic and Zepbound pens containing insulin to 63 hospitalisations and 3 deaths across seven states. FDA extends import alerts to tirzepatide and retatrutide as CBP mail seizures run about four times their 2027 level.
Head-to-head trial finds Lilly's Foundayo pill non-inferior to injectable semaglutide, and the label is updated. Pills become the majority of all US incretin users by year end.

Novo Nordisk and HHS announce an authorised-generic semaglutide pill and pen at $49–69 cash and $55 to public payers from January 2030. Novo settles patent suits allowing licensed generics from March 2031.

Year-end package creates a Part D obesity benefit for generic-tier incretins, a 90% Medicaid match and free health-centre provision for the uninsured. CBO scores ~$18B net over ten years, versus $41B for the 2027 proposal.

Federal data show hip-fracture admissions among women over 75 up about 3% since 2028, reversing a decade of decline. Medicare makes DXA scans and strength-training referrals a condition of continued coverage for users over 65.

FDA adds anhedonia to incretin labels after a randomised substudy finds it in 8% of users versus 3% on placebo. The same month, EEOC settles its ADA charges with a requirement that premium programmes accommodate dose reduction.

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer for a drug that measurably raises hip-fracture risk in the population it newly covers. The DXA safeguard depends on scanner capacity that has 8–14-week waits in Florida and Arizona.

Public programmes pay for cheap semaglutide while Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide stay in the cash and commercial tier. The two tiers now produce visibly different bodies, and the March 2031 generic entry will cheapen semaglutide further without touching the premium tier.

Legitimate $49 product drained the semaglutide gray market, but counterfeit Zepbound pens and 'research' retatrutide powders are growing among people who want the dense look without paying for it, and personal-importation enforcement is still porous.
Medicaid adolescent coverage of the generic widened the group of teenagers medicated during peak bone-mass years before the pediatric bone study has reported.

prose.headline: The $49 Body: Washington Made Thin Free. Now Muscle Is What Money Buys.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about seventeen American adults in a hundred take an incretin drug. That is barely more than two years ago, but the people taking it have changed and so has who pays. Since January, a Novo Nordisk authorised generic of semaglutide, the same molecule in a plain box, sells for forty-nine to sixty-nine dollars a month. Most people take it as the pill. The pill now matches the pen, and Lilly's Foundayo showed the same in a head-to-head trial last year. Wegovy's list price is still printed at $1,349.

The cheap box came with a law. Last December, in a year-end package, Congress did what it had refused to do in 2027. It let Medicare pay for obesity treatment, but only for the generic. The copay is ten dollars or less. Medicaid gets ninety cents of federal money on every dollar it spends on the drug, and thirty-eight states took it. Health centres hand bottles to the uninsured for free. CBO scored the package at about eighteen billion dollars over ten years, less than half the 2027 figure, because the price had fallen so far. The public programmes now pay for more users than employers do. In two years the bottom income third went from eleven percent on the drug to fifteen.

The price fell, and the bone warning arrived at the same time. In March federal data showed hip-fracture admissions among women over seventy-five rising for the first time in a decade, about three percent, perhaps nine thousand extra broken hips a year. Medicare now makes users over sixty-five get a bone scan and a strength-training referral before their second year of coverage. Scanners in Florida are booked into next season. YMCAs teach lifting to women in their seventies so they can keep their prescriptions.

Thinness used to mark money. Now a public programme hands it out, and the marker has moved. In Houston clinics people say "Medicaid thin" for a soft, slightly stooped leanness. In River Oaks the gyms sell density, with quarterly scan printouts that members compare. The bodies at the top are lean and hard. They come from Lilly's tirzepatide, from retatrutide, the triple agonist approved last year at a thousand dollars a month, and from coaches and protein. Below that tier is a counterfeit market that has moved upmarket. People who want the hard look without the price buy fake Zepbound pens and research-grade retatrutide by mail. A batch of fake pens filled with insulin put sixty-three people in hospital last year.

The flatness now has a name. In June the FDA added anhedonia to the labels after a randomised study found it in eight users in a hundred, against three in a hundred on placebo. Most people never needed the study. They say "going grey", and they manage it. A third of pill users admit they skip days or step down a dose to feel more. Families keep a no-pill Sunday for the church dinner. Endocrinologists point out that semaglutide stays in the body for a week, so the Sunday skip barely changes anything. Nobody stops doing it. The employers who sold "steadiness" two years ago have mostly dropped the word. An EEOC settlement now requires them to accommodate dose reduction, and California banned premiums tied to adherence.

The food industry is now losing volume in the baskets it thought were safe: dollar stores, SNAP, regional bottlers. Spirits keep sliding. The refusal coalition lost its best argument when the drug became cheap and now argues about bones and sedation. Next March licensed Indian generics arrive and the price falls again. Nobody expects that to touch Lilly's premium tier.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Ortega wakes at 5:40 in her daughter's back bedroom in San Antonio. She takes the white tablet with the small paper cup of water, no more than the pharmacist said, then sits on the bed edge and waits the thirty minutes before coffee. Her granddaughter calls it the meditation. The bottle says SEMAGLUTIDE TABLETS 25 MG, no Wegovy on it, and her Part D copay is five dollars. Her cafeteria pension couldn't have covered the old price.

At nine the YMCA class meets: eleven women and one widower, all with the same green referral slip. The instructor is twenty-six and calls them 'my density girls.' Marisol deadlifts a kettlebell that weighs less than the turkey she used to carry at Thanksgiving. Her scan is booked for February. The letter says coverage continues upon documentation.

Lunch is half a torta. She wraps the other half for Danny, her grandson, who lifts at a gym near Fort Sam and is very lean, very hard. He gets his vials from a Telegram man. They come labelled RESEARCH USE ONLY, and his forearms tingle at night. When she asks, he tells her not to worry, Grandma, it's the good stuff.

At church on Wednesday there is a potluck. She has already decided this is a skip day. Her doctor told her one day does nothing. She skips it anyway, and eats a second tamal, and laughs too loudly at Father Ruiz's joke. She feels, briefly, like the colour has come back up.

At home her daughter, on Zepbound through work, is already asleep.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo's US revenue fell even as its US unit volume roughly doubled
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: adult users rose only from ~43M to ~45M and Lilly holds the premium tier, so Novo's units cannot roughly double without an implausible share swing or dosing change, and the candidate shows neither.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Modelling attributes ~8,000–10,000 excess hip fractures a year to incretin use, against ~300,000 total.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the observed 3% rise is confined to women 75+, who are only part of ~300k fractures, so it cannot produce excess equal to ~3% of all fractures. The prose compounds this by tying the 'nine thousand' to the women-75+ rise.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pills become the majority of all US incretin users by year end.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: orals were under 40% of users in 2028 because established injectable users stay put, and the $49 pill only launches Jan 2030. Flipping the whole user base to majority-oral by end-2029 is asserted, not shown.

rationale.badness: Access broadens and conditioning retreats (California and EEOC rulings, Part D at $0–10), so autonomy and epistemic harms ease relative to 2028. Remaining harms: a measurable hip-fracture rise in older women (safety_ledger lean-mass entry), DXA queues of 8–14 weeks, a falls signal, and a hardened dense-versus-'Medicaid thin' class split. Adolescent exposure widens through Medicaid, and flatness is now a normalised, named complaint. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden one, so about 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable to fields and events. Generic collapse comes via the Novo authorised generic (an event), public expansion via the Part D, Medicaid and HRSA package, oral parity via the Foundayo trial, and the bone wave, counterfeits, stratification and mainstream complaint are all visible. new_indications stays empty, and the retatrutide and survodutide approvals are new products on allowed timelines. mechanism: most changes have chains (price drop collapses semaglutide counterfeits; free provision lifts bottom-third use; bone data trigger the DXA condition). Some are asserted: the oral majority by end-2029 (claim 3), an FDA anhedonia label in the same month as the study, and the MariTide filing with no event. magnitude: all headline figures sit inside the envelope (17.0 on drug, 24.5 ever-used, income and age checks, payer mix summing to 45.4M, CBO and Medicaid and HRSA arithmetic). Gaps remain: Novo units doubling against +5% users (claim 1), the hip-fracture attribution mismatch (claim 2), and '~20M public users × $55' treating all public users as generic-tier.
rationale.generativity: The prose runs through a believable day for Marisol: the pill and paper cup, the YMCA 'density girls' class with green referral slips, the skip-day potluck, Danny's Telegram-sourced research vials with tingling forearms, and a daughter on Zepbound. The world fields add concrete texture, such as 'Medicaid thin' in Houston, River Oaks DXA printouts, 'going grey', and 'thaw' memoirs. Characters, scenes and conflicts are clearly implied across class and generation.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Offsets of ~$18B from bill-attributable brand-to-generic switching and ~$1B medical offsets give ≈ $18B net.
